label: DrayTek Vigor 2766 G.Fast / VDSL2 VPN router
description: DrayTek Vigor 2766 - SoHo G.Fast, VDSL2, ADSL and Ethernet WAN VPN router (base wired model: no Wi-Fi, no VoIP ports) with one RJ-11 DSL port carrying G.Fast/VDSL2 35b/ADSL2+, four Gigabit Ethernet RJ-45 ports one of which can be reassigned as the Ethernet WAN2, a USB 2.0 port for a 3G/4G modem, SPI firewall with content filtering, four LAN subnets with port-based or 802.1Q VLANs and two VPN tunnels. 950 Mbps firewall throughput on Ethernet WAN, 24 W maximum from a 12 V external supply.
notes: The series datasheet's physical interface block reads '**WAN1: G.Fast / VDSL2 / VDSL2 35b / ADSL2+, RJ-11**', '**WAN2/LAN Switchable Port: 1x Gigabit Ethernet**', '**WAN3: USB 2.0**', and the summary bullet says '**4 Gigabit LAN Ports**' with '**4 LAN Subnets**'. As on the Vigor 2765, the Ethernet WAN is **not a fifth socket** - it is one of the four RJ-45s reassigned - so the spec declares `dsl0` plus four LAN ports and leaves the reassignment to this note. Declaring a separate WAN2 would show five RJ-45s on a four-port box. The **G.Fast** capability is the difference from the 2765: the same RJ-11 socket terminates a G.Fast line, so a lab modelling a G.Fast tail can use this chassis rather than the older one. Speed on the DSL port is a line-rate placeholder: G.Fast/VDSL2 rates depend on the loop, and the datasheet quotes none. This is the `V2766-K` wired base: AC1300 radios belong to `V2766AC-K` and the two FXS ports to `V2766VAC-K`, so neither is declared. 12 V external PSU, no PoE.
